toolUseResult.originalFile:
#!/bin/bash
# Neumann CLI Installer
# Usage: curl -sSfL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Shadylukin/Neumann/main/install.sh | bash
#
# Environment variables:
#   NEUMANN_INSTALL_DIR - Installation directory (default: /usr/local/bin or ~/.local/bin)
#   NEUMANN_VERSION     - Specific version to install (default: latest)
#   NEUMANN_NO_MODIFY_PATH - Set to 1 to skip PATH modification
#   NEUMANN_SKIP_EXTRAS - Set to 1 to skip completions and man page installation

set -euo pipefail

REPO="Shadylukin/Neumann"
BINARY_NAME="neumann"
GITHUB_API="https://api.github.com"
GITHUB_RELEASES="https://github.com/${REPO}/releases"

# Colors for output
RED='\033[0;31m'
GREEN='\033[0;32m'
YELLOW='\033[0;33m'
BLUE='\033[0;34m'
NC='\033[0m' # No Color

info() {
    echo -e "${BLUE}==>${NC} $1"
}

success() {
    echo -e "${GREEN}==>${NC} $1"
}

warn() {
    echo -e "${YELLOW}Warning:${NC} $1"
}

error() {
    echo -e "${RED}Error:${NC} $1" >&2
    exit 1
}

detect_platform() {
    local os arch

    os=$(uname -s | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')
    arch=$(uname -m)

    case "$os" in
        linux)
            os="linux"
            ;;
        darwin)
            os="darwin"
            ;;
        mingw*|msys*|cygwin*)
            error "Windows detected. Please download from GitHub releases or use: winget install neumann"
            ;;
        *)
            error "Unsupported operating system: $os"
            ;;
    esac

    case "$arch" in
        x86_64|amd64)
            arch="x86_64"
            ;;
        arm64|aarch64)
            arch="aarch64"
            ;;
        *)
            error "Unsupported architecture: $arch"
            ;;
    esac

    echo "${os}-${arch}"
}

get_latest_version() {
    local version
    version=$(curl -sSfL "${GITHUB_API}/repos/${REPO}/releases/latest" 2>/dev/null | \
        grep '"tag_name"' | \
        sed -E 's/.*"tag_name": *"([^"]+)".*/\1/')

    if [ -z "$version" ]; then
        return 1
    fi
    echo "$version"
}

download_binary() {
    local version="$1"
    local platform="$2"
    local tmpdir="$3"

    local archive_name="neumann-${version}-${platform}.tar.gz"
    local url="${GITHUB_RELEASES}/download/${version}/${archive_name}"

    info "Downloading ${archive_name}..."

    if curl -sSfL -o "${tmpdir}/${archive_name}" "$url" 2>/dev/null; then
        info "Extracting archive..."
        tar -xzf "${tmpdir}/${archive_name}" -C "$tmpdir"

        if [ -f "${tmpdir}/${BINARY_NAME}" ]; then
            return 0
        fi
    fi

    return 1
}

build_from_source() {
    local tmpdir="$1"

    info "Pre-built binary not available for this platform"
    info "Building from source..."

    # Check for Rust
    if ! command -v cargo &>/dev/null; then
        error "Cargo not found. Please install Rust from https://rustup.rs"
    fi

    # Check Rust version
    local rust_version
    rust_version=$(rustc --version | sed -E 's/rustc ([0-9]+\.[0-9]+).*/\1/')
    local required="1.75"

    if [ "$(printf '%s\n' "$required" "$rust_version" | sort -V | head -n1)" != "$required" ]; then
        error "Rust $required or later is required (found $rust_version)"
    fi

    # Clone and build
    info "Cloning repository..."
    git clone --depth 1 "https://github.com/${REPO}.git" "${tmpdir}/neumann" || \
        error "Failed to clone repository"

    cd "${tmpdir}/neumann"

    info "Building release binary (this may take a few minutes)..."
    cargo build --release --package neumann || \
        error "Build failed"

    cp "target/release/${BINARY_NAME}" "${tmpdir}/${BINARY_NAME}"

    # Copy completions if available
    local completions_dir
    completions_dir=$(find target/release/build -path "*neumann_shell*/out/completions" -type d 2>/dev/null | head -1)
    if [ -n "$completions_dir" ] && [ -d "$completions_dir" ]; then
        mkdir -p "${tmpdir}/completions"
        cp "$completions_dir"/* "${tmpdir}/completions/" 2>/dev/null || true
    fi

    # Copy man page if available
    local man_dir
    man_dir=$(find target/release/build -path "*neumann_shell*/out/man" -type d 2>/dev/null | head -1)
    if [ -n "$man_dir" ] && [ -d "$man_dir" ]; then
        mkdir -p "${tmpdir}/man"
        cp "$man_dir"/* "${tmpdir}/man/" 2>/dev/null || true
    fi
}

get_install_dir() {
    # Use environment variable if set
    if [ -n "${NEUMANN_INSTALL_DIR:-}" ]; then
        echo "$NEUMANN_INSTALL_DIR"
        return
    fi

    # Try /usr/local/bin first (requires sudo)
    if [ -w "/usr/local/bin" ]; then
        echo "/usr/local/bin"
        return
    fi

    # Fall back to ~/.local/bin
    local local_bin="${HOME}/.local/bin"
    mkdir -p "$local_bin"
    echo "$local_bin"
}

install_binary() {
    local tmpdir="$1"
    local install_dir="$2"
    local binary_path="${tmpdir}/${BINARY_NAME}"

    if [ ! -f "$binary_path" ]; then
        error "Binary not found at ${binary_path}"
    fi

    # Check if we need sudo
    if [ ! -w "$install_dir" ]; then
        info "Installing to ${install_dir} (requires sudo)..."
        sudo install -m 755 "$binary_path" "${install_dir}/${BINARY_NAME}"
    else
        info "Installing to ${install_dir}..."
        install -m 755 "$binary_path" "${install_dir}/${BINARY_NAME}"
    fi
}

install_extras() {
    local tmpdir="$1"

    # Skip if disabled
    if [ "${NEUMANN_SKIP_EXTRAS:-0}" = "1" ]; then
        return
    fi

    # Install shell completions
    if [ -d "${tmpdir}/completions" ]; then
        # Bash completions
        local bash_completions="/usr/local/share/bash-completion/completions"
        if [ -d "$bash_completions" ] || sudo mkdir -p "$bash_completions" 2>/dev/null; then
            if [ -f "${tmpdir}/completions/neumann.bash" ]; then
                sudo cp "${tmpdir}/completions/neumann.bash" "$bash_completions/neumann" 2>/dev/null || true
            fi
        fi

        # Zsh completions
        local zsh_completions="/usr/local/share/zsh/site-functions"
        if [ -d "$zsh_completions" ] || sudo mkdir -p "$zsh_completions" 2>/dev/null; then
            if [ -f "${tmpdir}/completions/_neumann" ]; then
                sudo cp "${tmpdir}/completions/_neumann" "$zsh_completions/_neumann" 2>/dev/null || true
            fi
        fi

        # Fish completions
        local fish_completions="/usr/local/share/fish/vendor_completions.d"
        if [ -d "$fish_completions" ] || sudo mkdir -p "$fish_completions" 2>/dev/null; then
            if [ -f "${tmpdir}/completions/neumann.fish" ]; then
                sudo cp "${tmpdir}/completions/neumann.fish" "$fish_completions/neumann.fish" 2>/dev/null || true
            fi
        fi

        info "Shell completions installed (restart shell to activate)"
    fi

    # Install man page
    if [ -f "${tmpdir}/man/neumann.1" ]; then
        local man_dir="/usr/local/share/man/man1"
        if [ -d "$man_dir" ] || sudo mkdir -p "$man_dir" 2>/dev/null; then
            sudo cp "${tmpdir}/man/neumann.1" "$man_dir/" 2>/dev/null && \
                info "Man page installed (try: man neumann)" || true
        fi
    fi
}

add_to_path() {
    local install_dir="$1"

    # Skip if disabled
    if [ "${NEUMANN_NO_MODIFY_PATH:-0}" = "1" ]; then
        return
    fi

    # Skip if already in PATH
    if echo "$PATH" | tr ':' '\n' | grep -qx "$install_dir"; then
        return
    fi

    # Skip if it's a standard directory
    if [ "$install_dir" = "/usr/local/bin" ] || [ "$install_dir" = "/usr/bin" ]; then
        return
    fi

    local shell_config
    if [ -n "${ZSH_VERSION:-}" ] || [ -f "${HOME}/.zshrc" ]; then
        shell_config="${HOME}/.zshrc"
    elif [ -n "${BASH_VERSION:-}" ] || [ -f "${HOME}/.bashrc" ]; then
        shell_config="${HOME}/.bashrc"
    else
        warn "Could not determine shell config file"
        warn "Please add ${install_dir} to your PATH manually"
        return
    fi

    local path_line="export PATH=\"${install_dir}:\$PATH\""

    if ! grep -qF "$install_dir" "$shell_config" 2>/dev/null; then
        {
            echo ""
            echo "# Added by Neumann installer"
            echo "$path_line"
        } >> "$shell_config"
        info "Added ${install_dir} to PATH in ${shell_config}"
        warn "Please restart your shell or run: source ${shell_config}"
    fi
}

check_existing_installation() {
    if command -v "$BINARY_NAME" &>/dev/null; then
        local current_version
        current_version=$("$BINARY_NAME" --version 2>/dev/null | head -n1 || echo "unknown")
        info "Found existing installation: ${current_version}"
    fi
}

main() {
    echo ""
    echo "  Neumann CLI Installer"
    echo "  ====================="
    echo ""

    # Detect platform
    local platform
    platform=$(detect_platform)
    info "Detected platform: ${platform}"

    # Map platform to target triple
    local target
    case "$platform" in
        linux-x86_64)
            target="x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu"
            ;;
        darwin-x86_64)
            target="x86_64-apple-darwin"
            ;;
        darwin-aarch64)
            target="aarch64-apple-darwin"
            ;;
        *)
            error "Unknown platform: ${platform}"
            ;;
    esac

    # Check for existing installation
    check_existing_installation

    # Get version to install
    local version="${NEUMANN_VERSION:-}"
    if [ -z "$version" ]; then
        info "Fetching latest version..."
        version=$(get_latest_version) || true
    fi

    # Create temporary directory
    local tmpdir
    tmpdir=$(mktemp -d)
    trap 'rm -rf "$tmpdir"' EXIT

    # Try to download pre-built binary
    local binary_available=false
    if [ -n "$version" ]; then
        info "Installing version: ${version}"
        if download_binary "$version" "$target" "$tmpdir"; then
            binary_available=true
        fi
    fi

    # Fall back to building from source
    if [ "$binary_available" = false ]; then
        build_from_source "$tmpdir"
    fi

    # Install
    local install_dir
    install_dir=$(get_install_dir)
    install_binary "$tmpdir" "$install_dir"

    # Install extras (completions, man page)
    install_extras "$tmpdir"

    # Update PATH if needed
    add_to_path "$install_dir"

    # Verify installation
    echo ""
    success "Neumann CLI installed successfully!"
    echo ""

    if [ -x "${install_dir}/${BINARY_NAME}" ]; then
        info "Installed to: ${install_dir}/${BINARY_NAME}"
        info "Version: $("${install_dir}/${BINARY_NAME}" --version 2>/dev/null || echo 'unknown')"
    fi

    echo ""
    echo "  Get started:"
    echo "    neumann              # Start interactive shell"
    echo "    neumann --help       # Show help"
    echo "    neumann -c 'query'   # Execute single query"
    echo ""
    echo "  Documentation:"
    echo "    https://github.com/${REPO}"
    echo ""
}

main "$@"

---
name: Documentation

"on":
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'docs/**'
      - '**/src/**/*.rs'
      - '**/Cargo.toml'
      - '.github/workflows/docs.yml'
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - 'docs/**'
      - '**/src/**/*.rs'
  workflow_dispatch:

env:
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  rustdoc:
    name: Build API Docs
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        # v4.2.2
        uses: actions/checkout@de0fac2e4500dabe0009e67214ff5f5447ce83dd

      - name: Install Rust
        # nightly
        uses: >-
          dtolnay/rust-toolchain@f7ccc83f9ed1e5b9c81d8a67d7ad1a747e22a561
        with:
          toolchain: nightly
          components: rust-docs

      - name: Cache cargo
        # v2.7.8
        uses: >-
          Swatinem/rust-cache@779680da715d629ac1d338a641029a2f4372abb5

      - name: Install protoc
        run: >-
          sudo apt-get update &&
          sudo apt-get install -y protobuf-compiler

      - name: Build rustdoc
        run: |
          RUSTDOCFLAGS="--cfg docsrs -Dwarnings" \
            cargo +nightly doc \
            --workspace \
            --no-deps \
            --all-features \
            -Zunstable-options \
            -Zrustdoc-scrape-examples

      - name: Upload rustdoc
        # v4.6.2
        uses: >-
          actions/upload-artifact@b7c566a772e6b6bfb58ed0dc250532a479d7789f
        with:
          name: rustdoc
          path: target/doc
          retention-days: 7

  mdbook:
    name: Build Book
    needs: [benchmarks]
    if: ${{ always() }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        # v4.2.2
        uses: actions/checkout@de0fac2e4500dabe0009e67214ff5f5447ce83dd

      - name: Download bench-docs
        # v4.3.0
        uses: >-
          actions/download-artifact@37930b1c2abaa49bbe596cd826c3c89aef350131
        continue-on-error: true
        with:
          name: bench-docs
          path: docs/book/src/reference/benchmarks/

      - name: Install mdBook
        run: |
          mkdir -p ~/.local/bin
          BASE="https://github.com/rust-lang/mdBook/releases/download"
          VER="v0.4.52"
          ARCHIVE="mdbook-$VER-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz"
          curl -sSL "$BASE/$VER/$ARCHIVE" | tar -xz -C ~/.local/bin
          cargo install mdbook-mermaid@0.12.6 \
            mdbook-admonish \
            mdbook-linkcheck

      - name: Build book
        working-directory: docs/book
        run: |
          mdbook-mermaid install .
          mdbook-admonish install .
          mdbook build

      - name: Check links
        working-directory: docs/book
        run: mdbook-linkcheck --standalone

      - name: Upload book
        # v4.6.2
        uses: >-
          actions/upload-artifact@b7c566a772e6b6bfb58ed0dc250532a479d7789f
        with:
          name: book
          path: docs/book-output
          retention-days: 7

  bench-run:
    name: Bench ${{ matrix.group }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 45
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name == 'push'
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - group: store-core
            packages: --package tensor_store
            benches: >-
              --bench tensor_store_bench
              --bench wal_bench
            filter: >-
              ^(put|get|scan|concurrent|mixed|bloom|
              sparse|snapshot|metadata|delta|
              kmeans|tiered|wal)
          - group: store-hnsw
            packages: --package tensor_store
            benches: >-
              --bench tensor_store_bench
              --bench hnsw_concurrent_bench
            filter: '^hnsw'
          - group: parsers
            packages: >-
              --package tensor_compress
              --package neumann_parser
            filter: '.'
          - group: engines
            packages: >-
              --package relational_engine
              --package graph_engine
              --package vector_engine
            filter: '.'
          - group: cache
            packages: --package tensor_cache
            filter: '.'
          - group: specialized
            packages: >-
              --package tensor_vault
              --package tensor_blob
              --package tensor_checkpoint
              --package tensor_unified
            filter: '.'
          - group: distributed
            packages: >-
              --package tensor_chain
              --package query_router
              --package neumann
              --package neumann_server
            filter: '.'
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        # v4.2.2
        uses: actions/checkout@de0fac2e4500dabe0009e67214ff5f5447ce83dd

      - name: Install Rust
        # stable
        uses: >-
          dtolnay/rust-toolchain@f7ccc83f9ed1e5b9c81d8a67d7ad1a747e22a561
        with:
          toolchain: stable

      - name: Cache cargo
        # v2.7.8
        uses: >-
          Swatinem/rust-cache@779680da715d629ac1d338a641029a2f4372abb5

      - name: Install protoc, mold, and clang
        run: >-
          sudo apt-get update &&
          sudo apt-get install -y protobuf-compiler mold clang

      - name: Run benchmarks (quick mode)
        env:
          CARGO_TARGET_X86_64_UNKNOWN_LINUX_GNU_LINKER: clang
          CARGO_TARGET_X86_64_UNKNOWN_LINUX_GNU_RUSTFLAGS: >-
            -Clink-arg=-fuse-ld=mold
        run: >-
          cargo bench
          ${{ matrix.packages }}
          ${{ matrix.benches || '--bench ''*''' }}
          --
          --noplot
          --warm-up-time 1
          --measurement-time 2
          --sample-size 10
          --nresamples 500
          '${{ matrix.filter }}'

      - name: Upload Criterion output
        # v4.6.2
        uses: >-
          actions/upload-artifact@b7c566a772e6b6bfb58ed0dc250532a479d7789f
        with:
          name: criterion-${{ matrix.group }}
          path: target/criterion
          retention-days: 7

  benchmarks:
    name: Generate Benchmark Docs
    needs: [bench-run]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    if: ${{ always() && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        # v4.2.2
        uses: actions/checkout@de0fac2e4500dabe0009e67214ff5f5447ce83dd

      - name: Download all Criterion outputs
        # v4.3.0
        uses: >-
          actions/download-artifact@37930b1c2abaa49bbe596cd826c3c89aef350131
        with:
          pattern: criterion-*
          path: target/criterion
          merge-multiple: true

      - name: Install jq and bc
        run: >-
          sudo apt-get update &&
          sudo apt-get install -y jq bc

      - name: Generate benchmark summary
        run: |
          chmod +x scripts/generate-bench-docs.sh
          ./scripts/generate-bench-docs.sh

      - name: Upload updated benchmark docs
        # v4.6.2
        uses: >-
          actions/upload-artifact@b7c566a772e6b6bfb58ed0dc250532a479d7789f
        with:
          name: bench-docs
          path: docs/book/src/reference/benchmarks/
          retention-days: 7

      - name: Upload Criterion reports
        # v4.6.2
        uses: >-
          actions/upload-artifact@b7c566a772e6b6bfb58ed0dc250532a479d7789f
        with:
          name: criterion-reports
          path: target/criterion
          retention-days: 7

      - name: Upload baseline for PR comparisons
        # v4.6.2
        uses: >-
          actions/upload-artifact@b7c566a772e6b6bfb58ed0dc250532a479d7789f
        with:
          name: criterion-baseline
          path: target/criterion/**/new/estimates.json
          retention-days: 30

  deploy:
    name: Deploy to GitHub Pages
    needs: [rustdoc, mdbook, benchmarks]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name == 'push'
    permissions:
      pages: write
      id-token: write
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
    steps:
      - name: Download book
        # v4.3.0
        uses: >-
          actions/download-artifact@37930b1c2abaa49bbe596cd826c3c89aef350131
        with:
          name: book
          path: public/

      - name: Download rustdoc
        # v4.3.0
        uses: >-
          actions/download-artifact@37930b1c2abaa49bbe596cd826c3c89aef350131
        with:
          name: rustdoc
          path: public/api/

      - name: Download Criterion HTML reports
        # v4.3.0
        uses: >-
          actions/download-artifact@37930b1c2abaa49bbe596cd826c3c89aef350131
        continue-on-error: true
        with:
          name: criterion-reports
          path: public/benchmarks/

      - name: Setup Pages
        # v5.0.0
        uses: >-
          actions/configure-pages@983d7736d9b0ae728b81ab479565c72886d7745b

      - name: Upload artifact
        # v3.0.1
        uses: >-
          actions/upload-pages-artifact@7b1f4a764d45c48632c6b24a0339c27f5614fb0b
        with:
          path: public/

      - name: Deploy to GitHub Pages
        id: deployment
        # v4.0.5
        uses: >-
          actions/deploy-pages@d6db90164ac5ed86f2b6aed7e0febac5b3c0c03e

content.text:
Yes — `cargo install neumann-db` gives you the full interactive CLI shell (`neumann` binary). It includes all engines:

- **Relational** — SQL tables, joins, indexes, SIMD filtering
- **Graph** — nodes, edges, BFS, shortest path, pattern matching
- **Vector** — HNSW k-NN search, 15+ distance metrics
- **Vault** — AES-256-GCM encrypted secrets
- **Cache** — multi-layer LLM response cache
- **Blob** — content-addressable object storage
- **Checkpoint** — snapshots and restore
- **Chain** — Raft consensus, 2PC distributed transactions

Run `neumann` to get the interactive REPL, or `neumann --help` for CLI options.

If you want to embed Neumann as a library in a Rust project instead, add individual crates as dependencies (e.g., `tensor_store`, `query_router`, etc.).

1→# Neumann 2→ 3→

4→ 5→ 6→

7→ 8→Stop juggling five databases for one AI app. 9→ 10→Neumann stores your tables, graphs, and vectors in one place. 11→Query across all three in a single statement. 12→ 13→```sql 14→-- Find engineers similar to Alice who report to Bob 15→FIND NODE person 16→ WHERE role = 'engineer' 17→ SIMILAR TO 'user:alice' 18→ CONNECTED TO 'user:bob' 19→``` 20→ 21→One query. Relational filter + vector similarity + graph traversal. 22→ 23→[![CI](https://github.com/Shadylukin/Neumann/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/Shadylukin/Neumann/actions/workflows/ci.yml) 24→[![codecov](https://codecov.io/gh/Shadylukin/Neumann/graph/badge.svg)](https://codecov.io/gh/Shadylukin/Neumann) 25→[![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-BSL--1.1-blue.svg)](LICENSE) 26→[![Rust](https://img.shields.io/badge/Rust-1.75+-orange.svg)](https://www.rust-lang.org) 27→[![Discord](https://img.shields.io/badge/Discord-Join-7289da.svg)](https://discord.gg/uN3KbAyKvw) 28→[![Sponsor](https://img.shields.io/badge/Sponsor-EA4AAA?logo=githubsponsors&logoColor=fff)](https://github.com/sponsors/Shadylukin) 29→ 30→## Why Neumann 31→ 32→**Three engines, one system.** Store a table, connect entities in a graph, 33→and search by vector similarity -- without moving data between systems. 34→No ETL, no sync, no glue code. 35→ 36→**Semantic consensus.** Concurrent writes to different fields auto-merge. 37→The consensus layer classifies conflicts geometrically rather than treating 38→all concurrent writes as errors. 39→ 40→```text 41→Alice updates email, Bob updates photo (same user, same time). 42→Traditional DB: conflict, manual resolution. 43→Neumann: auto-merges (different fields = orthogonal changes). 44→``` 45→ 46→**AI-native by design.** Built-in embedding storage, semantic caching for 47→LLM responses, and encrypted vault for secrets. The query language 48→understands similarity, not just equality. 49→ 50→## Use Cases 51→ 52→**RAG** -- Store documents with embeddings and relationships. Semantic 53→search follows graph links automatically. 54→ 55→**Agent memory** -- Conversation history with vector recall across 56→sessions. Cache repeated LLM calls to cut API costs. 57→ 58→**Knowledge graphs** -- Combine structured data with semantic similarity. 59→Find entities by what they *mean*, not just what they match. 60→ 61→**Access control** -- Graph-based permissions. Query results respect 62→who's asking. 63→ 64→See [Use Cases](docs/book/src/tutorials/use-cases.md) for worked examples 65→with Python, TypeScript, and the CLI. 66→ 67→## Quick Start 68→ 69→```bash 70→curl -sSfL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Shadylukin/Neumann/main/install.sh | bash 71→neumann 72→``` 73→ 74→```sql 75→-- Relational 76→CREATE TABLE users (id INT, name TEXT, role TEXT); 77→INSERT users id=1, name='Alice', role='engineer'; 78→SELECT * FROM users WHERE role = 'engineer'; 79→ 80→-- Graph 81→NODE CREATE person {name: 'Alice'}; 82→NODE CREATE person {name: 'Bob'}; 83→EDGE CREATE 1 -> 2 : reports_to; 84→ 85→-- Vector 86→EMBED STORE 'user:alice' [0.1, 0.2, 0.3]; 87→SIMILAR 'user:alice' TOP 5; 88→``` 89→ 90→More install methods (Homebrew, Cargo, Docker, source) in the 91→[Installation Guide](docs/book/src/how-to/installation.md). 92→Full walkthrough in the 93→[Quick Start Tutorial](docs/book/src/tutorials/quick-start.md). 94→ 95→## SDKs 96→ 97→**Python** 98→ 99→```bash 100→pip install neumann-db 101→``` 102→ 103→```python 104→from neumann import NeumannClient 105→client = NeumannClient.connect("localhost:9200") 106→result = client.execute("SELECT * FROM users") 107→``` 108→ 109→**TypeScript** 110→ 111→```bash 112→npm install @scrunchee/client 113→``` 114→ 115→```typescript 116→import { NeumannClient } from '@scrunchee/client'; 117→const client = await NeumannClient.connect("localhost:9200"); 118→const result = await client.execute("SELECT * FROM users"); 119→``` 120→ 121→Full tutorials: 122→[Python](docs/book/src/tutorials/python-sdk.md) | 123→[TypeScript](docs/book/src/tutorials/typescript-sdk.md) 124→ 125→## Dashboard 126→ 127→![Neumann Dashboard](images/dash.png) 128→*Web dashboard with system status and query terminal* 129→ 130→![Graph Visualization](images/graph.png) 131→*Interactive graph visualization with force-directed layout* 132→ 133→## Documentation 134→ 135→| I want to... | Go to | 136→|---|---| 137→| Follow a tutorial | [Quick Start](docs/book/src/tutorials/quick-start.md), [RAG in 5 Minutes](docs/book/src/tutorials/five-minute-rag.md), [Knowledge Graph](docs/book/src/tutorials/knowledge-graph.md) | 138→| Solve a specific problem | [How-to Guides](docs/book/src/how-to/installation.md) (30+ guides covering storage, graphs, vectors, security, deployment) | 139→| Look up syntax or config | [Query Language](docs/book/src/reference/query-language.md), [Configuration](docs/book/src/reference/configuration.md), [Error Types](docs/book/src/reference/error-types.md) | 140→| Understand the architecture | [Design Overview](docs/book/src/explanation/architecture-overview.md), [Consensus](docs/book/src/explanation/consensus-protocols.md), [HNSW](docs/book/src/explanation/hnsw-algorithm.md) | 141→ 142→[Full table of contents](docs/book/src/SUMMARY.md) | 143→[Rustdoc API Reference](https://shadylukin.github.io/Neumann/) 144→ 145→## Performance 146→ 147→Benchmarked on Apple M-series silicon: 148→ 149→- **3.8M reads/sec, 2.0M writes/sec** (in-memory, no durability) 150→- **22K durable writes/sec** with group commit, 260/sec with fsync 151→- **150us vector similarity** (HNSW, 10K embeddings, 128-dim) 152→- **52M conflict checks/sec** via sparse delta comparison 153→ 154→[Full benchmarks](docs/book/src/reference/benchmarks/index.md) 155→ 156→## Status 157→ 158→Neumann is pre-1.0 (v0.3.1). Core engines have 95%+ test coverage and 159→139 fuzz targets. Single-node is production-ready. Multi-node consensus 160→has comprehensive testing (loom, proptest, deterministic simulation) but 161→needs more real-world validation. 162→ 163→See the [roadmap](ROADMAP.md) for where we're headed -- native 164→embeddings, natural language queries, and AI-native analytics. 165→ 166→## The Name 167→ 168→John von Neumann unified code and data in the stored-program architecture. 169→Neumann unifies structure, relationships, and semantics. 170→ 171→## License 172→ 173→Licensed under the [Business Source License 1.1](LICENSE). 174→ 175→## Author 176→ 177→Built by [Lukin Ackroyd](https://scrunchee.ai) in Auckland, New Zealand. 178→ 179→Neumann is the infrastructure layer for [Scrunchee](https://scrunchee.ai). 180→

    42→detect_platform() {

    45→    os=$(uname -s | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')

    63→    case "$arch" in

    94→
    95→    local archive_name="neumann-${version}-${platform}.tar.gz"
    96→    local url="${GITHUB_RELEASES}/download/${version}/${archive_name}"
    97→
    98→    info "Downloading ${archive_name}..."
    99→
   100→    if curl -sSfL -o "${tmpdir}/${archive_name}" "$url" 2>/dev/null; then

   112→build_from_source() {
   113→    local tmpdir="$1"
   114→
   115→    info "Pre-built binary not available for this platform"
   116→    info "Building from source..."
   117→
   118→    # Check for Rust
   119→    if ! command -v cargo &>/dev/null; then
   120→        error "Cargo not found. Please install Rust from https://rustup.rs"
   121→    fi
   122→
   123→    # Check Rust version
   124→    local rust_version
   125→    rust_version=$(rustc --version | sed -E 's/rustc ([0-9]+\.[0-9]+).*/\1/')
   126→    local required="1.75"
   127→
   128→    if [ "$(printf '%s\n' "$required" "$rust_version" | sort -V | head -n1)" != "$required" ]; then
   129→        error "Rust $required or later is required (found $rust_version)"
   130→    fi
   131→
   132→    # Clone and build
   133→    info "Cloning repository..."
   134→    git clone --depth 1 "https://github.com/${REPO}.git" "${tmpdir}/neumann" || \
   135→        error "Failed to clone repository"
   136→
   137→    cd "${tmpdir}/neumann"
   138→
   139→    info "Building release binary (this may take a few minutes)..."
   140→    cargo build --release --package neumann-db || \
   141→        error "Build failed"
   142→
   143→    cp "target/release/${BINARY_NAME}" "${tmpdir}/${BINARY_NAME}"

   145→    # Copy completions if available
   146→    local completions_dir
   147→    completions_dir=$(find target/release/build -path "*neumann_shell*/out/completions" -type d 2>/dev/null | head -1)

   152→
   153→    # Copy man page if available

   156→    if [ -n "$man_dir" ] && [ -d "$man_dir" ]; then
   157→        mkdir -p "${tmpdir}/man"
   158→        cp "$man_dir"/* "${tmpdir}/man/" 2>/dev/null || true
   159→    fi
   160→}

   162→get_install_dir() {
   163→    # Use environment variable if set
   164→    if [ -n "${NEUMANN_INSTALL_DIR:-}" ]; then
   165→        echo "$NEUMANN_INSTALL_DIR"

   167→    fi
   168→
   169→    # Try /usr/local/bin first (requires sudo)
   170→    if [ -w "/usr/local/bin" ]; then

   181→install_binary() {

   183→    local install_dir="$2"

   186→    if [ ! -f "$binary_path" ]; then

   190→    # Check if we need sudo
   191→    if [ ! -w "$install_dir" ]; then

   193→        sudo install -m 755 "$binary_path" "${install_dir}/${BINARY_NAME}"

   196→        install -m 755 "$binary_path" "${install_dir}/${BINARY_NAME}"

   200→install_extras() {

   203→    # Skip if disabled

   206→    fi

   208→    # Install shell completions

   212→        if [ -d "$bash_completions" ] || sudo mkdir -p "$bash_completions" 2>/dev/null; then
   213→            if [ -f "${tmpdir}/completions/neumann.bash" ]; then

   247→add_to_path() {
   248→    local install_dir="$1"
   249→
   250→    # Skip if disabled
   251→    if [ "${NEUMANN_NO_MODIFY_PATH:-0}" = "1" ]; then
   252→        return
   253→    fi
   254→
   255→    # Skip if already in PATH
   256→    if echo "$PATH" | tr ':' '\n' | grep -qx "$install_dir"; then
   257→        return
   258→    fi
   259→
   260→    # Skip if it's a standard directory
   261→    if [ "$install_dir" = "/usr/local/bin" ] || [ "$install_dir" = "/usr/bin" ]; then
   262→        return
   263→    fi
   264→
   265→    local shell_config
   266→    if [ -n "${ZSH_VERSION:-}" ] || [ -f "${HOME}/.zshrc" ]; then
   267→        shell_config="${HOME}/.zshrc"
   268→    elif [ -n "${BASH_VERSION:-}" ] || [ -f "${HOME}/.bashrc" ]; then
   269→        shell_config="${HOME}/.bashrc"
   270→    else
   271→        warn "Could not determine shell config file"
   272→        warn "Please add ${install_dir} to your PATH manually"
   273→        return
   274→    fi
   275→
   276→    local path_line="export PATH=\"${install_dir}:\$PATH\""
   277→
   278→    if ! grep -qF "$install_dir" "$shell_config" 2>/dev/null; then
   279→        {
   280→            echo ""
   281→            echo "# Added by Neumann installer"
   282→            echo "$path_line"
   283→        } >> "$shell_config"
   284→        info "Added ${install_dir} to PATH in ${shell_config}"
   285→        warn "Please restart your shell or run: source ${shell_config}"
   286→    fi
   287→}

   328→    # Get version to install

   330→    if [ -z "$version" ]; then

   335→    # Create temporary directory

   340→    # Try to download pre-built binary

Cases](tutorials/use-cases.md) | 20→| Understand the design | [Architecture Overview](explanation/architecture-overview.md) | 21→| Use the Python SDK | [Python Quickstart](tutorials/python-sdk.md) | 22→| Use the TypeScript SDK | [TypeScript Quickstart](tutorials/typescript-sdk.md) | 23→| Look up a command | [Query Language Reference](reference/query-language.md) | 24→ 25→## What Makes Neumann Different 26→ 27→**One system, three engines.** Store a table, connect entities in a graph, and 28→search by vector similarity without moving data between systems. 29→ 30→```sql 31→-- Relational 32→CREATE TABLE documents (id INT PRIMARY KEY, title TEXT, author TEXT); 33→INSERT INTO documents VALUES (1, 'Intro to ML', 'Alice'); 34→ 35→-- Graph 36→NODE CREATE topic { name: 'machine-learning' } 37→ENTITY CONNECT 'doc-1' -> 'topic-ml' : covers 38→ 39→-- Vector 40→EMBED STORE 'doc-1' [0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4] 41→ 42→-- Cross-engine: find similar documents connected to a topic 43→SIMILAR 'doc-1' LIMIT 5 CONNECTED TO 'topic-ml' 44→``` 45→ 46→**Encrypted vault.** Store secrets with AES-256-GCM encryption and graph-based 47→access control. 48→ 49→**LLM cache.** Cache LLM responses with exact and semantic matching to reduce 50→API costs. 51→ 52→**Built-in consensus.** Raft-based distributed consensus with 2PC transactions 53→for multi-node deployments. 54→ 55→## Architecture 56→ 57→```text 58→ 65→ +-------------------+ 66→ | 67→ +----------+---------+---------+----------+ 68→ | | | | | 69→ relational graph vector tensor_ tensor_ 70→ _engine _engine _engine _vault _cache 71→ | | | | | 72→ +----------+---------+---------+----------+ 73→ | 74→ +-------------------+ 75→ | tensor_store | Core storage (HNSW, sharded B-trees) 76→ +-------------------+ 77→``` 78→ 79→Additional subsystems: `tensor_blob` (S3-style blob storage), `tensor_chain` 80→(blockchain with Raft), `tensor_checkpoint` (snapshots), `tensor_compress` 81→(tensor train decomposition). 82→ 83→## Getting Started 84→ 85→- 1→# Installation
     2→
     3→Multiple installation methods are available depending on your needs.
     4→
     5→## Quick Install (Recommended)
     6→
     7→The easiest way to install Neumann is using the install script:
     8→
     9→```bash
    10→curl -sSfL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Shadylukin/Neumann/main/install.sh | bash
    11→```
    12→
    13→This script will:
    14→
    15→- Detect your platform (Linux x86_64, macOS x86_64, macOS ARM64)
    16→- Download a pre-built binary if available
    17→- Fall back to building from source if needed
    18→- Install to `/usr/local/bin` or `~/.local/bin`
    19→- Install shell completions and man pages
    20→
    21→### Environment Variables
    22→
    23→| Variable | Description |
    24→| --- | --- |
    25→| `NEUMANN_INSTALL_DIR` | Custom installation directory |
    26→| `NEUMANN_VERSION` | Install a specific version (e.g., `v0.1.0`) |
    27→| `NEUMANN_NO_MODIFY_PATH` | Set to `1` to skip PATH modification |
    28→| `NEUMANN_SKIP_EXTRAS` | Set to `1` to skip completions and man page installation |
    29→
    30→## Homebrew (macOS/Linux)
    31→
    32→```bash
    33→brew tap Shadylukin/tap
    34→brew install neumann
    35→```
    36→
    37→## Cargo (crates.io)
    38→
    39→If you have Rust installed:
    40→
    41→```bash
    42→cargo install neumann_shell
    43→```
    44→
    45→To install the gRPC server:
    46→
    47→```bash
    48→cargo install neumann_server
    49→```
    50→
    51→## Docker
    52→
    53→### Interactive CLI
    54→
    55→```bash
    56→docker run -it shadylukinack/neumann:latest
    57→```
    58→
    59→### Server Mode
    60→
    61→```bash
    62→docker run -d -p 9200:9200 -v neumann-data:/var/lib/neumann shadylukinack/neumann:server
    63→```
    64→
    65→### Docker Compose
    66→
    67→```bash
    68→# Clone the repository
    69→git clone https://github.com/Shadylukin/Neumann.git
    70→cd Neumann
    71→
    72→# Start the server
    73→docker compose up -d neumann-server
    74→
    75→# Run the CLI
    76→docker compose run --rm neumann-cli
    77→```
    78→
    79→## From Source
    80→
    81→### Requirements
    82→
    83→- Rust 1.75 or later
    84→- Cargo (included with Rust)
    85→- Git
    86→- protobuf compiler (for gRPC)
    87→
    88→### Build Steps
    89→
    90→```bash
    91→# Clone the repository
    92→git clone https://github.com/Shadylukin/Neumann.git
    93→cd Neumann
    94→
    95→# Build in release mode
    96→cargo build --release --package neumann_shell
    97→
    98→# Install locally
    99→cargo install --path neumann_shell
   100→```
   101→
   102→### Run Tests
   103→
   104→```bash
   105→cargo test
   106→```
   107→
   108→## SDK Installation
   109→
   110→### Python
   111→
   112→```bash
   113→pip install neumann-db
   114→```
   115→
   116→For embedded mode (in-process database):
   117→
   118→```bash
   119→pip install neumann-db[native]
   120→```
   121→
   122→### TypeScript / JavaScript
   123→
   124→```bash
   125→npm install neumann-db
   126→```
   127→
   128→Or with yarn:
   129→
   130→```bash
   131→yarn add neumann-db
   132→```
   133→
   134→## Verify Installation
   135→
   136→```bash
   137→neumann --version
   138→```
   139→
   140→## Platform Support
   141→
   142→| Platform | Binary | Homebrew | Docker | Source |
   143→| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
   144→| Linux x86_64 | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
   145→| macOS x86_64 | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
   146→| macOS ARM64 (Apple Silicon) | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
   147→| Windows x86_64 | No | No | Yes | Experimental |
   148→
   149→## Troubleshooting
   150→
   151→### "command not found: neumann"
   152→
   153→The binary may not be in your PATH. Try:
   154→
   155→```bash
   156→# Check where it was installed
   157→which neumann || ls ~/.local/bin/neumann
   158→
   159→# Add to PATH if needed
   160→export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
   161→```
   162→
   163→### Build fails with protobuf errors
   164→
   165→Install the protobuf compiler:
   166→
   167→```bash
   168→# macOS
   169→brew install protobuf
   170→
   171→# Ubuntu/Debian
   172→sudo apt-get install protobuf-compiler
   173→
   174→# Fedora
   175→sudo dnf install protobuf-compiler
   176→```
   177→
   178→### Permission denied during install
   179→
   180→The installer tries `/usr/local/bin` first (requires sudo) then falls back
   181→to `~/.local/bin`. You can specify a custom directory:
   182→
   183→```bash
   184→NEUMANN_INSTALL_DIR=~/bin \
   185→  curl -sSfL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Shadylukin/Neumann/main/install.sh | bash
   186→```
   187→
   188→### Python SDK native module errors
   189→
   190→If you get errors about the native module, ensure you have a Rust toolchain:
   191→
   192→```bash
   193→curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf https://sh.rustup.rs | sh
   194→pip install neumann-db[native]
   195→```
   196→
   197→## Updating
   198→
   199→### Quick Install
   200→
   201→Re-run the install script to get the latest version:
   202→
   203→```bash
   204→curl -sSfL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Shadylukin/Neumann/main/install.sh | bash
   205→```
   206→
   207→### Homebrew
   208→
   209→```bash
   210→brew upgrade neumann
   211→```
   212→
   213→### Cargo
   214→
   215→```bash
   216→cargo install neumann_shell --force
   217→```
   218→
   219→### Python SDK
   220→
   221→```bash
   222→pip install --upgrade neumann-db
   223→```
   224→
   225→### TypeScript SDK
   226→
   227→```bash
   228→npm update neumann-db
   229→```
   230→
   231→## Uninstalling
   232→
   233→### Quick Install / Cargo
   234→
   235→```bash
   236→rm $(which neumann)
   237→```
   238→
   239→### Homebrew
   240→
   241→```bash
   242→brew uninstall neumann
   243→```
   244→
   245→### Docker
   246→
   247→```bash
   248→docker rmi shadylukinack/neumann:latest shadylukinack/neumann:server
   249→docker volume rm neumann-data
   250→```
   251→
   252→### Python SDK
   253→
   254→```bash
   255→pip uninstall neumann-db
   256→```
   257→
   258→### TypeScript SDK
   259→
   260→```bash
   261→npm uninstall neumann-db
   262→```
   263→
   264→## Next Steps

   267→- [Building from Source](building-from-source.md) - Development setup

1→# Deploy a Cluster
     2→
     3→## Single Node
     4→
     5→For development and testing:
     6→
     7→```bash
     8→neumann --data-dir ./data
     9→```
    10→
    11→## Cluster Deployment
    12→
    13→### Prerequisites
    14→
    15→- 3, 5, or 7 nodes (odd number for quorum)
    16→- Network connectivity between nodes
    17→- Synchronized clocks (NTP)
    18→
    19→### Starting the Cluster
    20→
    21→```bash
    22→# On each node, set environment and start
    23→export NEUMANN_CLUSTER_NODE_ID=node1
    24→export NEUMANN_CLUSTER_BIND_ADDR=0.0.0.0:9300
    25→export NEUMANN_CLUSTER_PEERS=node2=10.0.0.2:9300,node3=10.0.0.3:9300
    26→export NEUMANN_DATA_DIR=/var/lib/neumann
    27→neumann_server
    28→```
    29→
    30→See [Configuration](../reference/configuration.md) for the full list of
    31→environment variables and config file options.
    32→
    33→### Verify Cluster Health
    34→
    35→The server exposes a gRPC `Health.Check` service on port 9200:
    36→
    37→```bash
    38→grpcurl -plaintext localhost:9200 grpc.health.v1.Health/Check
    39→```
    40→
    41→## Docker Compose
    42→
    43→```yaml
    44→version: '3.8'
    45→services:
    46→  node1:
    47→    image: shadylukinack/neumann:latest
    48→    environment:
    49→      - NEUMANN_CLUSTER_NODE_ID=node1
    50→      - NEUMANN_CLUSTER_BIND_ADDR=0.0.0.0:9300
    51→      - NEUMANN_CLUSTER_PEERS=node2=node2:9300,node3=node3:9300
    52→      - NEUMANN_BIND_ADDR=0.0.0.0:9200
    53→      - NEUMANN_DATA_DIR=/var/lib/neumann
    54→    ports:
    55→      - "9200:9200"
    56→    volumes:
    57→      - node1-data:/var/lib/neumann
    58→
    59→  node2:
    60→    image: shadylukinack/neumann:latest
    61→    environment:
    62→      - NEUMANN_CLUSTER_NODE_ID=node2
    63→      - NEUMANN_CLUSTER_BIND_ADDR=0.0.0.0:9300
    64→      - NEUMANN_CLUSTER_PEERS=node1=node1:9300,node3=node3:9300
    65→      - NEUMANN_DATA_DIR=/var/lib/neumann
    66→    volumes:
    67→      - node2-data:/var/lib/neumann
    68→
    69→  node3:
    70→    image: shadylukinack/neumann:latest
    71→    environment:
    72→      - NEUMANN_CLUSTER_NODE_ID=node3
    73→      - NEUMANN_CLUSTER_BIND_ADDR=0.0.0.0:9300
    74→      - NEUMANN_CLUSTER_PEERS=node1=node1:9300,node2=node2:9300
    75→      - NEUMANN_DATA_DIR=/var/lib/neumann
    76→    volumes:
    77→      - node3-data:/var/lib/neumann
    78→
    79→volumes:
    80→  node1-data:
    81→  node2-data:
    82→  node3-data:
    83→```
    84→
    85→## Kubernetes
    86→
    87→Kustomize-based manifests are in `deploy/k8s/`. See `deploy/k8s/README.md`
    88→for full documentation.
    89→
    90→### Dev Deployment
    91→
    92→```bash
    93→kubectl apply -k deploy/k8s/overlays/dev/
    94→kubectl -n neumann get pods -w
    95→```
    96→
    97→### Production Deployment
    98→
    99→```bash
   100→kubectl apply -k deploy/k8s/overlays/production/
   101→```
   102→
   103→The production overlay adds server-side TLS (via cert-manager), higher
   104→resource limits, and 50Gi persistent volumes.
   105→
   106→### Connecting
   107→
   108→```bash
   109→kubectl -n neumann port-forward svc/neumann 9200:9200
   110→grpcurl -plaintext localhost:9200 grpc.health.v1.Health/Check
   111→```
   112→
   113→## Production Checklist
   114→
   115→- [ ] Odd number of nodes (3, 5, or 7)
   116→- [ ] Nodes in separate availability zones
   117→- [ ] NTP configured and synchronized
   118→- [ ] Firewall rules for ports 9200 (gRPC API) and 9300 (Raft)
   119→- [ ] Monitoring and alerting configured
   120→- [ ] Backup strategy in place
   121→- [ ] Resource limits set appropriately
   122→

1→# Quick Start
     2→
     3→Get up and running with Neumann in under 5 minutes. This guide walks you through
     4→relational queries, graph operations, vector search, and the cross-engine "wow"
     5→moment.
     6→
     7→## Start the Shell
     8→
     9→```bash
    10→# In-memory (data lost on exit)
    11→neumann
    12→
    13→# With persistence (recommended)
    14→neumann --wal-dir ./data
    15→```
    16→
    17→You will see:
    18→
    19→```text
    20→Neumann v0.1.0
    21→Type 'help' for available commands.
    22→neumann>
    23→```
    24→
    25→## 1. Relational Queries
    26→
    27→Create a table and insert some data:
    28→
    29→```sql
    30→CREATE TABLE people (id INT PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT, role TEXT, team TEXT);
    31→
    32→INSERT INTO people VALUES (1, 'Alice', 'Staff Engineer', 'Platform');
    33→INSERT INTO people VALUES (2, 'Bob', 'Engineering Manager', 'Platform');
    34→INSERT INTO people VALUES (3, 'Carol', 'Senior Engineer', 'ML');
    35→INSERT INTO people VALUES (4, 'Dave', 'Junior Engineer', 'Platform');
    36→```
    37→
    38→Query it:
    39→
    40→```sql
    41→SELECT * FROM people WHERE team = 'Platform';
    42→SELECT name, role FROM people ORDER BY name;
    43→SELECT team, COUNT(*) AS headcount FROM people GROUP BY team;
    44→```
    45→
    46→## 2. Graph Operations
    47→
    48→Create nodes with labels and properties:
    49→
    50→```sql
    51→NODE CREATE person { name: 'Alice', role: 'Staff Engineer' }
    52→NODE CREATE person { name: 'Bob', role: 'Engineering Manager' }
    53→NODE CREATE person { name: 'Carol', role: 'Senior Engineer' }
    54→NODE CREATE person { name: 'Dave', role: 'Junior Engineer' }
    55→```
    56→
    57→List the nodes to see their auto-generated IDs:
    58→
    59→```sql
    60→NODE LIST person
    61→```
    62→
    63→Create edges (replace the IDs with the actual values from NODE LIST):
    64→
    65→```sql
    66→EDGE CREATE 'alice-node-id' -> 'bob-node-id' : reports_to
    67→EDGE CREATE 'dave-node-id' -> 'bob-node-id' : reports_to
    68→EDGE CREATE 'alice-node-id' -> 'dave-node-id' : mentors
    69→```
    70→
    71→Traverse the graph:
    72→
    73→```sql
    74→NEIGHBORS 'bob-node-id' INCOMING : reports_to
    75→PATH SHORTEST 'dave-node-id' TO 'bob-node-id'
    76→```
    77→
    78→Run graph algorithms:
    79→
    80→```sql
    81→PAGERANK
    82→```
    83→
    84→## 3. Vector Search
    85→
    86→Store embeddings with string keys:
    87→
    88→```sql
    89→EMBED STORE 'alice' [0.9, 0.4, 0.1, 0.7, 0.6, 0.3]
    90→EMBED STORE 'bob' [0.6, 0.2, 0.1, 0.5, 0.3, 0.2]
    91→EMBED STORE 'carol' [0.3, 0.9, 0.1, 0.4, 0.8, 0.1]
    92→EMBED STORE 'dave' [0.4, 0.1, 0.2, 0.5, 0.2, 0.1]
    93→```
    94→
    95→Find similar items by key or by vector:
    96→
    97→```sql
    98→SIMILAR 'alice' LIMIT 3
    99→SIMILAR [0.8, 0.5, 0.1, 0.6, 0.5, 0.2] LIMIT 3 METRIC COSINE
   100→```
   101→
   102→Check what is stored:
   103→
   104→```sql
   105→SHOW EMBEDDINGS
   106→COUNT EMBEDDINGS
   107→```
   108→
   109→## 4. The Cross-Engine Moment
   110→
   111→This is where Neumann shines. Combine graph traversal with vector similarity
   112→in a single query:
   113→
   114→```sql
   115→SIMILAR 'alice' LIMIT 3 CONNECTED TO 'bob-node-id'
   116→```
   117→
   118→This finds embeddings similar to Alice's that are also connected to Bob in the
   119→graph. No joins across separate databases needed.
   120→
   121→Search across all engines with FIND:
   122→
   123→```sql
   124→FIND NODE person WHERE name = 'Alice'
   125→```
   126→
   127→Create unified entities that span relational, graph, and vector storage:
   128→
   129→```sql
   130→ENTITY CREATE 'project-x' { name: 'Project X', status: 'active' } EMBEDDING [0.5, 0.3, 0.7, 0.2, 0.4, 0.1]
   131→ENTITY GET 'project-x'
   132→```
   133→
   134→## 5. Persistence
   135→
   136→Save a checkpoint:
   137→
   138→```sql
   139→CHECKPOINT 'my-first-checkpoint'
   140→CHECKPOINTS
   141→```
   142→
   143→If you started with `--wal-dir`, your data persists across restarts. You can also
   144→save and load binary snapshots:
   145→
   146→```sql
   147→SAVE 'backup.bin'
   148→LOAD 'backup.bin'
   149→```

1→# Five-Minute Tutorial: Build a Mini RAG System
     2→
     3→This tutorial builds a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) knowledge base using
     4→all three engines. By the end, you will have documents stored relationally, linked
     5→in a graph, searchable by embeddings, and protected with vault secrets.
     6→
     7→## Prerequisites
     8→
     9→Start the shell with persistence:
    10→
    11→```bash
    12→neumann --wal-dir ./rag-data
    13→```
    14→
    15→## Step 1: Create the Document Store
    16→
    17→Use a relational table for structured document metadata:
    18→
    19→```sql
    20→CREATE TABLE documents (
    21→    id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    22→    title TEXT NOT NULL,
    23→    category TEXT,
    24→    author TEXT,
    25→    created TEXT
    26→);
    27→
    28→INSERT INTO documents VALUES (1, 'Intro to Neural Networks', 'ml', 'Alice', '2024-01-15');
    29→INSERT INTO documents VALUES (2, 'Transformer Architecture', 'ml', 'Bob', '2024-02-20');
    30→INSERT INTO documents VALUES (3, 'Database Indexing', 'systems', 'Carol', '2024-03-10');
    31→INSERT INTO documents VALUES (4, 'Vector Search at Scale', 'systems', 'Alice', '2024-04-05');
    32→INSERT INTO documents VALUES (5, 'Fine-Tuning LLMs', 'ml', 'Dave', '2024-05-12');
    33→INSERT INTO documents VALUES (6, 'Consensus Protocols', 'distributed', 'Eve', '2024-06-01');
    34→```
    35→
    36→Verify:
    37→
    38→```sql
    39→SELECT * FROM documents ORDER BY id;
    40→SELECT category, COUNT(*) FROM documents GROUP BY category;
    41→```
    42→
    43→## Step 2: Add Graph Relationships
    44→
    45→Create nodes for documents and topics, then link them:
    46→
    47→```sql
    48→NODE CREATE document { title: 'Intro to Neural Networks', doc_id: 1 }
    49→NODE CREATE document { title: 'Transformer Architecture', doc_id: 2 }
    50→NODE CREATE document { title: 'Database Indexing', doc_id: 3 }
    51→NODE CREATE document { title: 'Vector Search at Scale', doc_id: 4 }
    52→NODE CREATE document { title: 'Fine-Tuning LLMs', doc_id: 5 }
    53→NODE CREATE document { title: 'Consensus Protocols', doc_id: 6 }
    54→
    55→NODE CREATE topic { name: 'machine-learning' }
    56→NODE CREATE topic { name: 'systems' }
    57→NODE CREATE topic { name: 'distributed-systems' }
    58→```
    59→
    60→List nodes to get IDs:
    61→
    62→```sql
    63→NODE LIST document
    64→NODE LIST topic
    65→```
    66→
    67→Create edges linking documents to topics (use actual IDs from NODE LIST):
    68→
    69→```sql
    70→-- Documents 1, 2, 5 cover machine-learning
    71→-- Documents 3, 4 cover systems
    72→-- Documents 4, 6 cover distributed-systems
    73→-- Document 2 references document 1
    74→-- Document 5 references documents 1 and 2
    75→```
    76→
    77→Create citation relationships between documents:
    78→
    79→```sql
    80→EDGE CREATE 'doc2-id' -> 'doc1-id' : cites
    81→EDGE CREATE 'doc5-id' -> 'doc1-id' : cites
    82→EDGE CREATE 'doc5-id' -> 'doc2-id' : cites
    83→```
    84→
    85→Check the graph:
    86→
    87→```sql
    88→NEIGHBORS 'doc1-id' INCOMING : cites
    89→PATH SHORTEST 'doc5-id' TO 'doc1-id'
    90→```
    91→
    92→## Step 3: Store Embeddings
    93→
    94→Each document gets a vector representing its content. In a real system, you would
    95→generate these with an embedding model (e.g., OpenAI, Cohere, or a local model).
    96→Here we use hand-crafted 6-dimensional vectors:
    97→
    98→```sql
    99→-- [neural-nets, transformers, databases, vectors, llms, distributed]
   100→EMBED STORE 'doc-1' [0.9, 0.3, 0.1, 0.2, 0.2, 0.1]
   101→EMBED STORE 'doc-2' [0.7, 0.95, 0.1, 0.1, 0.4, 0.1]
   102→EMBED STORE 'doc-3' [0.1, 0.1, 0.95, 0.3, 0.0, 0.2]
   103→EMBED STORE 'doc-4' [0.2, 0.1, 0.5, 0.9, 0.1, 0.4]
   104→EMBED STORE 'doc-5' [0.6, 0.5, 0.1, 0.1, 0.95, 0.1]
   105→EMBED STORE 'doc-6' [0.1, 0.1, 0.3, 0.2, 0.1, 0.9]
   106→```
   107→
   108→Search by similarity:
   109→
   110→```sql
   111→-- Find documents similar to "Intro to Neural Networks"
   112→SIMILAR 'doc-1' LIMIT 3
   113→
   114→-- Search with a custom query vector (someone asking about transformers + LLMs)
   115→SIMILAR [0.5, 0.8, 0.1, 0.1, 0.7, 0.1] LIMIT 3 METRIC COSINE
   116→```
   117→
   118→## Step 4: Graph-Aware Semantic Search
   119→
   120→Combine vector similarity with graph connectivity. Find documents similar to a
   121→query vector that are also connected to a specific topic node:
   122→
   123→```sql
   124→SIMILAR [0.8, 0.6, 0.1, 0.1, 0.5, 0.1] LIMIT 3 CONNECTED TO 'ml-topic-id'
   125→```
   126→
   127→This is the core RAG pattern: retrieve relevant documents using embedding
   128→similarity, then filter by graph relationships for context-aware results.
   129→
   130→## Step 5: Protect API Keys with Vault
   131→
   132→Store the embedding API key securely:
   133→
   134→```sql
   135→VAULT SET 'openai_api_key' 'sk-proj-abc123...'
   136→VAULT SET 'cohere_api_key' 'co-xyz789...'
   137→VAULT GRANT 'alice' ON 'openai_api_key'
   138→```
   139→
   140→Retrieve when needed:
   141→
   142→```sql
   143→VAULT GET 'openai_api_key'
   144→VAULT LIST
   145→```
   146→
   147→## Step 6: Cache LLM Responses
   148→
   149→Initialize the cache and store responses to avoid repeated API calls:
   150→
   151→```sql
   152→CACHE INIT
   153→
   154→CACHE PUT 'what are transformers?' 'Transformers are a neural network architecture based on self-attention mechanisms...'
   155→
   156→CACHE SEMANTIC PUT 'explain attention mechanism' 'The attention mechanism allows models to focus on relevant parts of the input...' EMBEDDING [0.6, 0.9, 0.1, 0.1, 0.3, 0.1]
   157→```
   158→
   159→On subsequent queries, check the cache first:
   160→
   161→```sql
   162→CACHE GET 'what are transformers?'
   163→CACHE SEMANTIC GET 'how does attention work?' THRESHOLD 0.8
   164→```
   165→
   166→## Step 7: Checkpoint
   167→
   168→Save your work:
   169→
   170→```sql
   171→CHECKPOINT 'rag-setup-complete'
   172→CHECKPOINTS
   173→```
   174→
   175→## What You Built
   176→
   177→You now have a working RAG knowledge base with:
   178→
   179→1. **Structured metadata** in a relational table (searchable with SQL)
   180→2. **Semantic relationships** in a graph (topics, citations, authorship)
   181→3. **Vector embeddings** for similarity search
   182→4. **Graph-aware retrieval** combining similarity and structure
   183→5. **Encrypted secrets** for API key management
   184→6. **Response caching** to reduce LLM API costs
   185→7. **Checkpoint** for safe rollback
   186→

1→# Contributing to Neumann
     2→
     3→Thank you for your interest in contributing to Neumann! This project aims to
     4→provide unified tensor-based storage for the AI era, and we welcome
     5→contributions of all kinds.
     6→
     7→## Getting Started
     8→
     9→### Prerequisites
    10→
    11→- Rust 1.75 or later
    12→- Cargo (comes with Rust)
    13→- Git
    14→
    15→### Development Setup
    16→
    17→```bash
    18→# Clone the repository
    19→git clone https://github.com/Shadylukin/Neumann.git
    20→cd Neumann
    21→
    22→# Install the pre-commit hook
    23→./scripts/setup-hooks.sh
    24→
    25→# Build all crates
    26→cargo build
    27→
    28→# Run tests
    29→cargo test
    30→
    31→# Verify everything passes
    32→./scripts/pre-commit
    33→```
    34→
    35→### Project Structure
    36→
    37→Neumann is organized as a Cargo workspace with 11 crates:
    38→
    39→| Crate              | Purpose                      |
    40→| ------------------ | ---------------------------- |
    41→| `tensor_store`     | Core key-value storage layer |
    42→| `relational_engine`| SQL-like table operations    |
    43→| `graph_engine`     | Node/edge graph operations   |
    44→| `vector_engine`    | Embedding similarity search  |
    45→| `tensor_compress`  | Compression algorithms       |
    46→| `tensor_vault`     | Encrypted secret storage     |
    47→| `tensor_cache`     | LLM response caching         |
    48→| `tensor_blob`      | Chunked blob storage         |
    49→| `neumann_parser`   | Query language parser        |
    50→| `query_router`     | Unified query execution      |
    51→| `neumann_shell`    | Interactive CLI              |
    52→
    53→## How to Contribute
    54→
    55→### Reporting Bugs
    56→
    57→1. Check existing [issues](https://github.com/Shadylukin/Neumann/issues)
    58→   to avoid duplicates
    59→2. Use the bug report template
    60→3. Include:
    61→   - Rust version (`rustc --version`)
    62→   - Operating system
    63→   - Steps to reproduce
    64→   - Expected vs actual behavior
    65→
    66→### Suggesting Features
    67→
    68→1. Open an issue with the feature request template
    69→2. Describe the use case and motivation
    70→3. Be open to discussion about implementation approaches
    71→
    72→### Submitting Code
    73→
    74→1. Fork the repository
    75→2. Create a feature branch (`git checkout -b feature/your-feature`)
    76→3. Make your changes
    77→4. Ensure all checks pass:
    78→
    79→   ```bash
    80→   cargo fmt --check
    81→   cargo clippy -- -D warnings
    82→   cargo test
    83→   cargo doc --no-deps
    84→   ```
    85→
    86→5. Commit with a clear message (see below)
    87→6. Push and open a pull request
    88→
    89→## Code Standards
    90→
    91→### Style
    92→
    93→- Run `cargo fmt` before committing
    94→- No warnings from `cargo clippy -- -D warnings`
    95→- No emojis in code, comments, or commit messages
    96→- Prefer iterators over loops
    97→- Use `?` for error propagation
    98→- Keep functions small and focused
    99→
   100→### Testing

# Installation

Multiple installation methods are available depending on your needs.

## Quick Install (Recommended)

The easiest way to install Neumann is using the install script:

```bash
curl -sSfL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Shadylukin/Neumann/main/install.sh | bash
```

This script will:

- Detect your platform (Linux x86_64, macOS x86_64, macOS ARM64)
- Download a pre-built binary if available
- Fall back to building from source if needed
- Install to `/usr/local/bin` or `~/.local/bin`
- Install shell completions and man pages

### Environment Variables

| Variable | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `NEUMANN_INSTALL_DIR` | Custom installation directory |
| `NEUMANN_VERSION` | Install a specific version (e.g., `v0.1.0`) |
| `NEUMANN_NO_MODIFY_PATH` | Set to `1` to skip PATH modification |
| `NEUMANN_SKIP_EXTRAS` | Set to `1` to skip completions and man page installation |

## Homebrew (macOS/Linux)

```bash
brew tap Shadylukin/tap
brew install neumann
```

## Cargo (crates.io)

If you have Rust installed:

```bash
cargo install neumann_shell
```

To install the gRPC server:

```bash
cargo install neumann_server
```

## Docker

### Interactive CLI

```bash
docker run -it shadylukinack/neumann:latest
```

### Server Mode

```bash
docker run -d -p 9200:9200 -v neumann-data:/var/lib/neumann shadylukinack/neumann:server
```

### Docker Compose

```bash
# Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/Shadylukin/Neumann.git
cd Neumann

# Start the server
docker compose up -d neumann-server

# Run the CLI
docker compose run --rm neumann-cli
```

## From Source

### Requirements

- Rust 1.75 or later
- Cargo (included with Rust)
- Git
- protobuf compiler (for gRPC)

### Build Steps

```bash
# Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/Shadylukin/Neumann.git
cd Neumann

# Build in release mode
cargo build --release --package neumann_shell

# Install locally
cargo install --path neumann_shell
```

### Run Tests

```bash
cargo test
```

## SDK Installation

### Python

```bash
pip install neumann-db
```

For embedded mode (in-process database):

```bash
pip install neumann-db[native]
```

### TypeScript / JavaScript

```bash
npm install neumann-db
```

Or with yarn:

```bash
yarn add neumann-db
```

## Verify Installation

```bash
neumann --version
```

## Platform Support

| Platform | Binary | Homebrew | Docker | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Linux x86_64 | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| macOS x86_64 | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| macOS ARM64 (Apple Silicon) | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Windows x86_64 | No | No | Yes | Experimental |

## Troubleshooting

### "command not found: neumann"

The binary may not be in your PATH. Try:

```bash
# Check where it was installed
which neumann || ls ~/.local/bin/neumann

# Add to PATH if needed
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
```

### Build fails with protobuf errors

Install the protobuf compiler:

```bash
# macOS
brew install protobuf

# Ubuntu/Debian
sudo apt-get install protobuf-compiler

# Fedora
sudo dnf install protobuf-compiler
```

### Permission denied during install

The installer tries `/usr/local/bin` first (requires sudo) then falls back
to `~/.local/bin`. You can specify a custom directory:

```bash
NEUMANN_INSTALL_DIR=~/bin \
  curl -sSfL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Shadylukin/Neumann/main/install.sh | bash
```

### Python SDK native module errors

If you get errors about the native module, ensure you have a Rust toolchain:

```bash
curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf https://sh.rustup.rs | sh
pip install neumann-db[native]
```

## Updating

### Quick Install

Re-run the install script to get the latest version:

```bash
curl -sSfL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Shadylukin/Neumann/main/install.sh | bash
```

### Homebrew

```bash
brew upgrade neumann
```

### Cargo

```bash
cargo install neumann_shell --force
```

### Python SDK

```bash
pip install --upgrade neumann-db
```

### TypeScript SDK

```bash
npm update neumann-db
```

## Uninstalling

### Quick Install / Cargo

```bash
rm $(which neumann)
```

### Homebrew

```bash
brew uninstall neumann
```

### Docker

```bash
docker rmi shadylukinack/neumann:latest shadylukinack/neumann:server
docker volume rm neumann-data
```

### Python SDK

```bash
pip uninstall neumann-db
```

### TypeScript SDK

```bash
npm uninstall neumann-db
```

## Next Steps

- [Quick Start](../tutorials/quick-start.md) - Run your first queries
- [Building from Source](building-from-source.md) - Development setup

# Neumann

Stop juggling five databases for one AI app. Neumann stores your tables, graphs, and vectors in one place. Query across all three in a single statement. ```sql -- Find engineers similar to Alice who report to Bob FIND NODE person WHERE role = 'engineer' SIMILAR TO 'user:alice' CONNECTED TO 'user:bob' ``` One query. Relational filter + vector similarity + graph traversal. [![CI](https://github.com/Shadylukin/Neumann/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/Shadylukin/Neumann/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![codecov](https://codecov.io/gh/Shadylukin/Neumann/graph/badge.svg)](https://codecov.io/gh/Shadylukin/Neumann) [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-BSL--1.1-blue.svg)](LICENSE) [![Rust](https://img.shields.io/badge/Rust-1.75+-orange.svg)](https://www.rust-lang.org) [![Discord](https://img.shields.io/badge/Discord-Join-7289da.svg)](https://discord.gg/uN3KbAyKvw) [![Sponsor](https://img.shields.io/badge/Sponsor-EA4AAA?logo=githubsponsors&logoColor=fff)](https://github.com/sponsors/Shadylukin) ## Why Neumann **Three engines, one system.** Store a table, connect entities in a graph, and search by vector similarity -- without moving data between systems. No ETL, no sync, no glue code. **Semantic consensus.** Concurrent writes to different fields auto-merge. The consensus layer classifies conflicts geometrically rather than treating all concurrent writes as errors. ```text Alice updates email, Bob updates photo (same user, same time). Traditional DB: conflict, manual resolution. Neumann: auto-merges (different fields = orthogonal changes). ``` **AI-native by design.** Built-in embedding storage, semantic caching for LLM responses, and encrypted vault for secrets. The query language understands similarity, not just equality. ## Use Cases **RAG** -- Store documents with embeddings and relationships. Semantic search follows graph links automatically. **Agent memory** -- Conversation history with vector recall across sessions. Cache repeated LLM calls to cut API costs. **Knowledge graphs** -- Combine structured data with semantic similarity. Find entities by what they *mean*, not just what they match. **Access control** -- Graph-based permissions. Query results respect who's asking. See [Use Cases](docs/book/src/tutorials/use-cases.md) for worked examples with Python, TypeScript, and the CLI. ## Quick Start ```bash curl -sSfL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Shadylukin/Neumann/main/install.sh | bash neumann ``` ```sql -- Relational CREATE TABLE users (id INT, name TEXT, role TEXT); INSERT users id=1, name='Alice', role='engineer'; SELECT * FROM users WHERE role = 'engineer'; -- Graph NODE CREATE person {name: 'Alice'}; NODE CREATE person {name: 'Bob'}; EDGE CREATE 1 -> 2 : reports_to; -- Vector EMBED STORE 'user:alice' [0.1, 0.2, 0.3]; SIMILAR 'user:alice' TOP 5; ``` More install methods (Homebrew, Cargo, Docker, source) in the [Installation Guide](docs/book/src/how-to/installation.md). Full walkthrough in the [Quick Start Tutorial](docs/book/src/tutorials/quick-start.md). ## SDKs **Python** ```bash pip install neumann-db ``` ```python from neumann import NeumannClient client = NeumannClient.connect("localhost:9200") result = client.execute("SELECT * FROM users") ``` **TypeScript** ```bash npm install @scrunchee/client ``` ```typescript import { NeumannClient } from '@scrunchee/client'; const client = await NeumannClient.connect("localhost:9200"); const result = await client.execute("SELECT * FROM users"); ``` Full tutorials: [Python](docs/book/src/tutorials/python-sdk.md) | [TypeScript](docs/book/src/tutorials/typescript-sdk.md) ## Dashboard ![Neumann Dashboard](images/dash.png) *Web dashboard with system status and query terminal* ![Graph Visualization](images/graph.png) *Interactive graph visualization with force-directed layout* ## Documentation | I want to... | Go to | |---|---| | Follow a tutorial | [Quick Start](docs/book/src/tutorials/quick-start.md), [RAG in 5 Minutes](docs/book/src/tutorials/five-minute-rag.md), [Knowledge Graph](docs/book/src/tutorials/knowledge-graph.md) | | Solve a specific problem | [How-to Guides](docs/book/src/how-to/installation.md) (30+ guides covering storage, graphs, vectors, security, deployment) | | Look up syntax or config | [Query Language](docs/book/src/reference/query-language.md), [Configuration](docs/book/src/reference/configuration.md), [Error Types](docs/book/src/reference/error-types.md) | | Understand the architecture | [Design Overview](docs/book/src/explanation/architecture-overview.md), [Consensus](docs/book/src/explanation/consensus-protocols.md), [HNSW](docs/book/src/explanation/hnsw-algorithm.md) | [Full table of contents](docs/book/src/SUMMARY.md) | [Rustdoc API Reference](https://shadylukin.github.io/Neumann/) ## Performance Benchmarked on Apple M-series silicon: - **3.8M reads/sec, 2.0M writes/sec** (in-memory, no durability) - **22K durable writes/sec** with group commit, 260/sec with fsync - **150us vector similarity** (HNSW, 10K embeddings, 128-dim) - **52M conflict checks/sec** via sparse delta comparison [Full benchmarks](docs/book/src/reference/benchmarks/index.md) ## Status Neumann is pre-1.0 (v0.3.1). Core engines have 95%+ test coverage and 139 fuzz targets. Single-node is production-ready. Multi-node consensus has comprehensive testing (loom, proptest, deterministic simulation) but needs more real-world validation. See the [roadmap](ROADMAP.md) for where we're headed -- native embeddings, natural language queries, and AI-native analytics. ## The Name John von Neumann unified code and data in the stored-program architecture. Neumann unifies structure, relationships, and semantics. ## License Licensed under the [Business Source License 1.1](LICENSE). ## Author Built by [Lukin Ackroyd](https://scrunchee.ai) in Auckland, New Zealand. Neumann is the infrastructure layer for [Scrunchee](https://scrunchee.ai).

# Installation

Multiple installation methods are available depending on your needs.

## Quick Install (Recommended)

The easiest way to install Neumann is using the install script:

```bash
curl -sSfL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Shadylukin/Neumann/main/install.sh | bash
```

This script will:

- Detect your platform (Linux x86_64, macOS x86_64, macOS ARM64)
- Download a pre-built binary if available
- Fall back to building from source if needed
- Install to `/usr/local/bin` or `~/.local/bin`
- Install shell completions and man pages

### Environment Variables

| Variable | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `NEUMANN_INSTALL_DIR` | Custom installation directory |
| `NEUMANN_VERSION` | Install a specific version (e.g., `v0.1.0`) |
| `NEUMANN_NO_MODIFY_PATH` | Set to `1` to skip PATH modification |
| `NEUMANN_SKIP_EXTRAS` | Set to `1` to skip completions and man page installation |

## Homebrew (macOS/Linux)

```bash
brew tap Shadylukin/tap
brew install neumann
```

## Cargo (crates.io)

If you have Rust installed:

```bash
cargo install neumann_shell
```

To install the gRPC server:

```bash
cargo install neumann_server
```

## Docker

### Interactive CLI

```bash
docker run -it shadylukinack/neumann:latest
```

### Server Mode

```bash
docker run -d -p 9200:9200 -v neumann-data:/var/lib/neumann shadylukinack/neumann:server
```

### Docker Compose

```bash
# Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/Shadylukin/Neumann.git
cd Neumann

# Start the server
docker compose up -d neumann-server

# Run the CLI
docker compose run --rm neumann-cli
```

## From Source

### Requirements

- Rust 1.75 or later
- Cargo (included with Rust)
- Git
- protobuf compiler (for gRPC)

### Build Steps

```bash
# Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/Shadylukin/Neumann.git
cd Neumann

# Build in release mode
cargo build --release --package neumann_shell

# Install locally
cargo install --path neumann_shell
```

### Run Tests

```bash
cargo test
```

## SDK Installation

### Python

```bash
pip install neumann-db
```

For embedded mode (in-process database):

```bash
pip install neumann-db[native]
```

### TypeScript / JavaScript

```bash
npm install neumann-db
```

Or with yarn:

```bash
yarn add neumann-db
```

## Verify Installation

```bash
neumann --version
```

## Platform Support

| Platform | Binary | Homebrew | Docker | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Linux x86_64 | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| macOS x86_64 | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| macOS ARM64 (Apple Silicon) | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Windows x86_64 | No | No | Yes | Experimental |

## Troubleshooting

### "command not found: neumann"

The binary may not be in your PATH. Try:

```bash
# Check where it was installed
which neumann || ls ~/.local/bin/neumann

# Add to PATH if needed
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
```

### Build fails with protobuf errors

Install the protobuf compiler:

```bash
# macOS
brew install protobuf

# Ubuntu/Debian
sudo apt-get install protobuf-compiler

# Fedora
sudo dnf install protobuf-compiler
```

### Permission denied during install

The installer tries `/usr/local/bin` first (requires sudo) then falls back
to `~/.local/bin`. You can specify a custom directory:

```bash
NEUMANN_INSTALL_DIR=~/bin \
  curl -sSfL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Shadylukin/Neumann/main/install.sh | bash
```

### Python SDK native module errors

If you get errors about the native module, ensure you have a Rust toolchain:

```bash
curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf https://sh.rustup.rs | sh
pip install neumann-db[native]
```

## Updating

### Quick Install

Re-run the install script to get the latest version:

```bash
curl -sSfL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Shadylukin/Neumann/main/install.sh | bash
```

### Homebrew

```bash
brew upgrade neumann
```

### Cargo

```bash
cargo install neumann_shell --force
```

### Python SDK

```bash
pip install --upgrade neumann-db
```

### TypeScript SDK

```bash
npm update neumann-db
```

## Uninstalling

### Quick Install / Cargo

```bash
rm $(which neumann)
```

### Homebrew

```bash
brew uninstall neumann
```

### Docker

```bash
docker rmi shadylukinack/neumann:latest shadylukinack/neumann:server
docker volume rm neumann-data
```

### Python SDK

```bash
pip uninstall neumann-db
```

### TypeScript SDK

```bash
npm uninstall neumann-db
```

## Next Steps

- [Quick Start](../tutorials/quick-start.md) - Run your first queries
- [Building from Source](building-from-source.md) - Development setup

# Neumann

Stop juggling five databases for one AI app. Neumann stores your tables, graphs, and vectors in one place. Query across all three in a single statement. ```sql -- Find engineers similar to Alice who report to Bob FIND NODE person WHERE role = 'engineer' SIMILAR TO 'user:alice' CONNECTED TO 'user:bob' ``` One query. Relational filter + vector similarity + graph traversal. [![CI](https://github.com/Shadylukin/Neumann/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/Shadylukin/Neumann/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![codecov](https://codecov.io/gh/Shadylukin/Neumann/graph/badge.svg)](https://codecov.io/gh/Shadylukin/Neumann) [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-BSL--1.1-blue.svg)](LICENSE) [![Rust](https://img.shields.io/badge/Rust-1.75+-orange.svg)](https://www.rust-lang.org) [![Discord](https://img.shields.io/badge/Discord-Join-7289da.svg)](https://discord.gg/uN3KbAyKvw) [![Sponsor](https://img.shields.io/badge/Sponsor-EA4AAA?logo=githubsponsors&logoColor=fff)](https://github.com/sponsors/Shadylukin) ## Why Neumann **Three engines, one system.** Store a table, connect entities in a graph, and search by vector similarity -- without moving data between systems. No ETL, no sync, no glue code. **Semantic consensus.** Concurrent writes to different fields auto-merge. The consensus layer classifies conflicts geometrically rather than treating all concurrent writes as errors. ```text Alice updates email, Bob updates photo (same user, same time). Traditional DB: conflict, manual resolution. Neumann: auto-merges (different fields = orthogonal changes). ``` **AI-native by design.** Built-in embedding storage, semantic caching for LLM responses, and encrypted vault for secrets. The query language understands similarity, not just equality. ## Use Cases **RAG** -- Store documents with embeddings and relationships. Semantic search follows graph links automatically. **Agent memory** -- Conversation history with vector recall across sessions. Cache repeated LLM calls to cut API costs. **Knowledge graphs** -- Combine structured data with semantic similarity. Find entities by what they *mean*, not just what they match. **Access control** -- Graph-based permissions. Query results respect who's asking. See [Use Cases](docs/book/src/tutorials/use-cases.md) for worked examples with Python, TypeScript, and the CLI. ## Quick Start ```bash curl -sSfL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Shadylukin/Neumann/main/install.sh | bash neumann ``` ```sql -- Relational CREATE TABLE users (id INT, name TEXT, role TEXT); INSERT users id=1, name='Alice', role='engineer'; SELECT * FROM users WHERE role = 'engineer'; -- Graph NODE CREATE person {name: 'Alice'}; NODE CREATE person {name: 'Bob'}; EDGE CREATE 1 -> 2 : reports_to; -- Vector EMBED STORE 'user:alice' [0.1, 0.2, 0.3]; SIMILAR 'user:alice' TOP 5; ``` More install methods (Homebrew, Cargo, Docker, source) in the [Installation Guide](docs/book/src/how-to/installation.md). Full walkthrough in the [Quick Start Tutorial](docs/book/src/tutorials/quick-start.md). ## SDKs **Python** ```bash pip install neumann-db ``` ```python from neumann import NeumannClient client = NeumannClient.connect("localhost:9200") result = client.execute("SELECT * FROM users") ``` **TypeScript** ```bash npm install @scrunchee/client ``` ```typescript import { NeumannClient } from '@scrunchee/client'; const client = await NeumannClient.connect("localhost:9200"); const result = await client.execute("SELECT * FROM users"); ``` Full tutorials: [Python](docs/book/src/tutorials/python-sdk.md) | [TypeScript](docs/book/src/tutorials/typescript-sdk.md) ## Dashboard ![Neumann Dashboard](images/dash.png) *Web dashboard with system status and query terminal* ![Graph Visualization](images/graph.png) *Interactive graph visualization with force-directed layout* ## Documentation | I want to... | Go to | |---|---| | Follow a tutorial | [Quick Start](docs/book/src/tutorials/quick-start.md), [RAG in 5 Minutes](docs/book/src/tutorials/five-minute-rag.md), [Knowledge Graph](docs/book/src/tutorials/knowledge-graph.md) | | Solve a specific problem | [How-to Guides](docs/book/src/how-to/installation.md) (30+ guides covering storage, graphs, vectors, security, deployment) | | Look up syntax or config | [Query Language](docs/book/src/reference/query-language.md), [Configuration](docs/book/src/reference/configuration.md), [Error Types](docs/book/src/reference/error-types.md) | | Understand the architecture | [Design Overview](docs/book/src/explanation/architecture-overview.md), [Consensus](docs/book/src/explanation/consensus-protocols.md), [HNSW](docs/book/src/explanation/hnsw-algorithm.md) | [Full table of contents](docs/book/src/SUMMARY.md) | [Rustdoc API Reference](https://shadylukin.github.io/Neumann/) ## Performance Benchmarked on Apple M-series silicon: - **3.8M reads/sec, 2.0M writes/sec** (in-memory, no durability) - **22K durable writes/sec** with group commit, 260/sec with fsync - **150us vector similarity** (HNSW, 10K embeddings, 128-dim) - **52M conflict checks/sec** via sparse delta comparison [Full benchmarks](docs/book/src/reference/benchmarks/index.md) ## Status Neumann is pre-1.0 (v0.3.1). Core engines have 95%+ test coverage and 139 fuzz targets. Single-node is production-ready. Multi-node consensus has comprehensive testing (loom, proptest, deterministic simulation) but needs more real-world validation. See the [roadmap](ROADMAP.md) for where we're headed -- native embeddings, natural language queries, and AI-native analytics. ## The Name John von Neumann unified code and data in the stored-program architecture. Neumann unifies structure, relationships, and semantics. ## License Licensed under the [Business Source License 1.1](LICENSE). ## Author Built by [Lukin Ackroyd](https://scrunchee.ai) in Auckland, New Zealand. Neumann is the infrastructure layer for [Scrunchee](https://scrunchee.ai).
